A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Uncertainty-driven Embedding Convolution (UEC) work. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original MIRACL and MMTEB experiments, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative retrieval analysis, including additional task results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds comparator evaluations, classification AUROC results, embedding-alignment measurements, and similarity-metric comparisons.

M1.justification: The post-hoc Laplace approximation, uncertainty-weighted Gaussian convolution, and probit similarity procedure are retained. The corrected denominator in Eq. 4 matches v1 Appendix A.1, and the clarified mean normalization was already documented in v1 Appendix A.2; these do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same MIRACL languages, MS MARCO/SNLI fitting data, and MMTEB retrieval, classification, STS, bitext mining, clustering, and reranking coverage. The new alignment and similarity analyses reuse MIRACL and Wikipedia data already evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds GroVE on GTE-MB to the retrieval, classification, and STS comparisons, and Borda count to retrieval. New Appendix B.2 also evaluates KLD, 1-Wasserstein, 2-Wasserstein, and CSD against UEC similarity. These substantially expand the evaluated comparison methods while retaining the previous baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds classification AUROC and introduces pairwise CCA analysis on retained MIRACL/Wikipedia data and a similarity-runtime comparison normalized to UEC. The existing experiments retain their stated fitting sample counts, retrieval cutoffs, temperatures, and hyperparameter search ranges; changed scores do not establish reruns or revised settings.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.1 tests embedding-subspace overlap using CCA, addressing whether embeddings can reasonably be combined directly. Appendix B.2 tests alternative similarity functions for retrieval performance and efficiency. These add substantial diagnostic evidence; the original component ablation, coefficient heatmap, and challenging retrieval example remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty across experimental runs. The added AUROC and CCA scores are evaluation measurements, not new reporting of statistical uncertainty in the results.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes UEC's reported average nDCG@10 from 78.86 to 79.58 and AUC@10 from 66.05 to 67.61. UEC's STS22 score changes from 68.55 to 69.55, while weighted-ensemble Belebele nDCG changes from 95.66 to 93.64. Numerous GroVE, Borda, AUROC, CCA, and alternative-distance results are added. The original MIRACL, component-ablation, bitext, clustering, and reranking numerical results are retained.

T1.justification: v1 contains derivations of ensemble weights and similarity moments. v2 adds Theorem 1 on squared 2-Wasserstein approximation and Appendix A.3 with scaling assumptions, extensive derivations, a Jeffreys-divergence theorem, and ranking-equivalence claims. This substantially expands the formal theoretical content.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the similarity contribution from uncertainty-aware scoring that improves robustness to a theoretically grounded, efficient surrogate for distributional distances. Section 3.3 makes this concrete through a claimed bounded approximation and ranking guarantee. The original probabilistic-conversion and adaptive-ensemble contributions remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments connecting shared architectures, overlapping training data, normalization, and CCA overlap to the suitability of direct ensembling. It also interprets the new uncertainty evaluations and introduces concentrated-variance and heterogeneous-scale qualifications for its approximation guarantees. The previous text-only, diagonal-Laplace, and equal-dimensionality limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 specifies GTE-MB as the base for GroVE and supplies formulas for the newly evaluated distributional distances. Appendix C newly discloses LLM assistance with writing and experimental code. Existing Laplace-fitting instructions, hyperparameter ranges, and code/library access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 substantially broadens positioning against probabilistic multimodal methods, adding discussions of Chun's works, ProbVLM, hedged embeddings, compositional retrieval, and MAP while removing the earlier face-recognition, medical-imaging, and probabilistic language-image pre-training examples. Additional references support Wasserstein distances, alignment, CCA, and Borda. Section 4.2 also newly claims the first systematic MMTEB evaluation of merging and ensemble techniques.

P1.justification: v2 extensively revises the introduction, probabilistic-related-work discussion, similarity explanation, experimental narrative, and conclusion. It reorders classification and STS, moves coefficient analysis into MIRACL, places efficiency before ablation, and integrates the separate limitations and impact paragraphs into the conclusion. These are substantial narrative and structural edits beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: v2 changes the title block, running headers, typography, and page layout; expands the main tables with comparator columns/rows and AUROC rows; and adds CCA and similarity-comparison tables. Figure 2 is recolored, Figure 4 is relocated, and several captions and table headings are revised. Existing auxiliary tables are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful probabilistic/rank baselines and diagnostic comparisons, but introduces substantive reliability problems. Theorem 1's O(epsilon^2) claim conflicts with Eqs. 5–6 and 14: identical Gaussians with unit means and covariance epsilon I produce an O(epsilon) discrepancy despite zero Wasserstein distance. Appendix B.2 also claims best recall and lowest runtime despite Table 7 showing higher recall for 2-Wasserstein and faster CSD runtime. These empirical benefits and new theoretical/reporting defects leave the net quality direction uncertain.
